Petitioner  Versus The State of Jharkhand ... ...

CORAM: HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE ANUBHA RAWAT CHOUDHARY ---
For the Petitioner : Mr. Pratik Sen, Advocate For the State : Ms. Lily Sahay, Advocate  ---
 th 03/14 June 2024 1.
Learned counsel for the parties are present.

2. This revision application has been directed against the judgment dated 29.01.2024 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-I-cum-Children's Court, Hazaribagh in Criminal Appeal (Juvenile) No. 02 of 2024 whereby the appeal preferred by the petitioner has been dismissed.

The learned Principal Magistrate, Juvenile Justice Board, Hazaribagh has refused to release the petitioner on bail vide order dated 19.12.2023 in connection with Muffasil P.S. Case No. 332 of 2023 registered for offence under Sections 420/385/467/468/471/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 66(C)/67/67(A) of the Information Technology Act.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the present offence is the first office of the petitioner and the social investigation report has not been fully appreciated by the learned courts while refusing the bail to the petitioner.

The petitioner is 15 years of age and the social investigation report has been called for wherein it has been clearly indicated that the petitioner is a student of Class-IX in Amritnagar High School and has a positive attitude towards school and wants to continue his studies.
The petitioner is in custody since 26.11.2023.

sentences.text: 4. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State has opposed the prayer.
However, the aforesaid noting in connection with juvenile history of the petitioner in the social investigation report is not in dispute.

5. At this, the learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that he has taken instructions that the father of the petitioner who is also the pairvikar before this Court who has undertaken to take due care of the petitioner and the petitioner has expressed his willingness to join Hindi and English computer typing to develop additional skill in life so that he may become useful citizen and assimilate with the society at large.
6.

After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of this case, this Court finds that in the social investigation report it has specifically mentioned that the petitioner is a student of Class-IX in Amritnagar High School and he has positive attitude towards school and wants to continue his studies.

7. In such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that it is in the interest of the juvenile to continue his studies and he shall also undertake development of additional skill by learning Hindi and English computer typing.
The petitioner is only 15 years of age and it is his first offence.

This Court also finds that this aspect of the mater that the petitioner has a positive attitude in continuing his studies has not been considered by the learned courts and accordingly, the impugned orders call for interference.
8.

Accordingly, the impugned orders refusing bail to the petitioner are hereby set-aside and the petitioner is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rs. Twenty-Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Principal Magistrate, Juvenile Justice Board, Hazaribagh in connection with Muffasil P.S. Case No. 332 of 2023

subject to the following conditions: -
(i) One of the bailors would be his father and the other would be a close relative.
(ii) As per willingness expressed by the petitioner, the petitioner would join institute to learn Hindi and English computer typing.
(iii) The father of the petitioner would ensure that the petitioner continues his studies and attends the educational institution regularly.

(iv) The Probation Officer of the concerned district shall submit social investigation report of the petitioner on 26.09.2024 before the Principal Magistrate, learned Juvenile Justice Board, Hazaribagh.
Thereafter he would submit social investigation report of the petitioner at interval of three months.
9. This criminal revision application is accordingly disposed of.
